question: Consider the following news: 'CAQM Reviews Compliance Status Across NCR; Flying Squads Conducted 199 Inspections During May 30-June 13'. Which organization, scheme, or focus area is this news related to?
explanation: The news items states: "CAQM Reviews Compliance Status Across NCR; Flying Squads Conducted 199 Inspections During May 30-June 13". Source: PIB National (English). Detail: The 133rd meeting of the Enforcement Task Force (ETF) of the Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM) was held on 19.06.2026 to review enforcement actions, inspections and compliance status across the National Capital Region (NCR) for the reporting period from 30.05.2026 to 13.06.2026. During the 15-day reporting period, the Flying Squads of the Commission carried out 199 inspections and detected 66 violations across Construction & Demolition (C&D) sites, industrial units and Diesel Generator (DG) sets. Based on the inspection reports, closure of 04 units/projects, sealing of 29 DG sets, issuance of 12 directions/orders for compliance and imposition of Environmental Compensation (EC) in 02 cases have been proposed. Of the 199 inspections conducted, 10 were carried out at C&D sites, 94 in the industrial sector and 95 pertaining to DG sets. A total of 66 violations were reported, including 08 from C&D sites, 23 from the industrial sector and 35 relating to DG sets.

question: Consider the following news: 'Biodiversity Pays Back: India's ABS Framework Delivers Rs 145 Crore to Beneficiaries'. Which organization, scheme, or focus area is this news related to?
explanation: The news items states: "Biodiversity Pays Back: India's ABS Framework Delivers Rs 145 Crore to Beneficiaries". Source: PIB National (English). Detail: India's Access and Benefit Sharing (ABS) framework under the Biological Diversity Act, 2002 has mobilized more than Rs 266 crore towards benefit sharing and disbursed around Rs 145 crore to beneficiaries, demonstrating the country's leadership in ensuring fair and equitable sharing of benefits arising from the utilization of biological resources and associated knowledge. The National Biodiversity Authority (NBA) has realized over Rs 266 crore through the ABS mechanism since 2008, including Rs 21.26 crore during FY 2025-26. With an average annual realization of Rs 14.75 crore, the steady increase in collections reflects growing industry participation and compliance, reaffirming the success of India's pioneering ABS regime in channeling benefits from the use of biological resources back to conservation efforts and local communities. Under the Biological Diversity Act, 2002, benefits arising from the utilization of biological resources are shared with local communities, Biodiversity Management Committees (BMCs), farmers, traditional knowledge holders and other custodians of biodiversity. Since the operationalization of the ABS framework, the NBA has disbursed around Rs 145 crore in benefit-sharing payments, including Rs 78 crore during FY 2025-26.

question: Consider the following news: 'NMDC Accelerates Digitalisation and Sustainable Mining at Donimalai to Support 100 MTPA Vision'. Which organization, scheme, or focus area is this news related to?
explanation: The news items states: "NMDC Accelerates Digitalisation and Sustainable Mining at Donimalai to Support 100 MTPA Vision". Source: PIB National (English). Detail: During a recent visit to the Donimalai Complex, NMDC's senior management reviewed a series of strategic initiatives aimed at strengthening operational efficiency, promoting responsible mining practices and improving the quality of life of employees and surrounding communities. The visit provided an opportunity to assess the progress of key projects that are helping transform Donimalai into a future-ready mining complex while reinforcing NMDC's position as India's largest and a Responsible Iron Ore Producer. During the visit, the management reviewed ongoing capacity expansion and infrastructure development initiatives aimed at achieving a production target of 10 MTPA from the Kumaraswamy Mine and 17 MTPA from the Donimalai Complex. These production enhancements form a key part of NMDC's vision of becoming a 100 MTPA mining company. The management also reviewed initiatives for the utilization of iron ore containing up to 35% Fe, iron ore slimes and low-grade iron-bearing materials such as Banded Hematite Jasper (BHJ) and Banded Hematite Quartzite (BHQ). Traditionally, these resources had limited utilization and were treated as waste, despite containing valuable iron content. Through beneficiation and scientific mineral processing, NMDC is converting these underutilized resources into valuable raw material, recovering more iron ore from existing mines while reducing waste generation. The initiative supports sustainable mining practices, improves mineral conservation, reduces the environmental footprint of mining operations and contributes to the growing raw material requirements of India's steel sector.

question: Consider the following news: 'Government Notifies Expansion of Central Drugs Laboratory Functions at CCS-NIAH, Baghpat for Veterinary Vaccine Testing'. Which organization, scheme, or focus area is this news related to?
explanation: The news items states: "Government Notifies Expansion of Central Drugs Laboratory Functions at CCS-NIAH, Baghpat for Veterinary Vaccine Testing". Source: PIB National (English). Detail: In a notable step towards strengthening the country's veterinary biological testing infrastructure, the Government of India has notified amendments to the Drugs Rules, 1945, expanding the functions of the Central Drugs Laboratory (CDL) at the Chaudhary Charan Singh–National Institute of Animal Health (CCS-NIAH), Baghpat, Uttar Pradesh, for veterinary vaccine testing. The amendments have been notified vide Gazette Notification G.S.R. 65(E), dated the 28th January, 2026 in the Gazette of India, Extraordinary, Part II, section 3, sub-section (i) under the provisions of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940. The notification is in line with the Government's ongoing efforts to augment vaccine and biological testing capacity in the country and further strengthen the regulatory framework for ensuring the quality, safety and efficacy of veterinary vaccines. Prior to this amendment, CCS-NIAH was notified for testing only two veterinary vaccines. With the latest notification, the scope of testing at the institute has been substantially expanded, enabling it to test 42 veterinary vaccines. These include vaccines used for the prevention and control of diseases such as Canine Distemper, Canine Coronavirus, Duck Plague, Fowl Pox, Salmonella and Tetanus, among others, affecting dogs, horses, poultry and other livestock.

Detail: This editorial is based on "NFHS-6 reveals progress amid nutrition challenges" published in The Hindu on 19/06/2026. question: Consider the following news: 'Ashtalakshmi – The North-East at the Heart of India’s Growth Story'. Which organization, scheme, or focus area is this news related to?
explanation: The news items states: "Ashtalakshmi – The North-East at the Heart of India’s Growth Story". Source: PIB Lucknow (English). Detail: Over the past twelve years, the North-East has witnessed a remarkable shift in its development landscape. This change has been driven by sustained policy support, infrastructure expansion, and inclusive development initiatives. Improved road, rail, air, and digital connectivity have reduced geographic isolation. They have also strengthened regional integration and economic access. At the same time, major gains in access to water, sanitation, housing, healthcare, and education have improved quality of life. These improvements are visible across both urban and rural communities. The region has also emerged as a key pillar of India’s clean energy transition and Act East vision. This shift has been supported by investments in hydropower, gas infrastructure, and cross-border connectivity. Together, these efforts position Ashtalakshmi as a model of sustainable and inclusive development within Viksit Bharat. Where hills reach up to meet the clouds, and rivers inspire music, art and literature, India’s North East tells a story of possibility. Home to eight distinct states, the region is collectively known as “Ashtalakshmi”. In Indian tradition, Goddess Lakshmi symbolises happiness, health, prosperity and good fortune.
